title: Evaluating APT Specimen Survivability: Site-specific Post-FIB Ar Ion Milling in Controlled Environments
content: Correlative studies that combine electron microscopy and atom probe tomography (APT) offer invaluable insights into the microstructural and compositional details of materials. However, the complexity of these techniques, particularly in sample preparation and data acquisition, presents challenges. Achieving high APT specimen survivability is desirable when statistically reliable results are required. Several approaches to improve APT specimen survivability have been explored, including surface depositions on bulk specimens [1], in situ deposition techniques after specimen preparation at ambient [2] or cryogenic conditions [3], and broad Ar ion milling as a post-focused ion beam (FIB) polishing step [4]. These methods primarily address the degradation of the specimen surface and subsurface quality caused by Ga ion implantation during FIB milling, hydrocarbon contamination from electron imaging, and environmental degradation during sample transfer. Careful sample preparation under controlled environmental conditions is essential to mitigate these issues and enhance APT specimen survivability. Our previous work [5-6] demonstrated the effectiveness of Ar ion beam milling techniques in reducing surface damage and oxidation under controlled environments. Here, we investigate the enhancement of APT specimen survivability by incorporating a site-specific concentrated Ar ion milling step following FIB preparation in a controlled environment workflow.
